entries.title: II Samuel 14:1
segments:
The king's heart was toward Absalom; he wished for some pretext to bring him back. 
 
Courtiers, and those who covet royal favor, are quick to discern the inclinations of rulers, and skillful in devising means and presenting inducements to gratify them.

entries.title: II Samuel 14:2
segments:
Tekoah; in Judah, a few miles south-east of Bethlehem. 
 
When great men and those in authority are set upon accomplishing their selfish objects, they will generally find agents deceitful and wicked enough to aid them.

entries.title: II Samuel 14:4
segments: Flatterers and those who are engaged in artful projects, are often most complaisant and respectful to those whose favor they seek, and whom they are aiming to deceive.

entries.title: II Samuel 14:5
segments: Compassion towards the distressed and desires to grant relief should be regulated by correct knowledge and sound judgment.

entries.title: II Samuel 14:7
segments: Quench my coal; destroy her son.

entries.title: II Samuel 14:8
segments:
Give charge concerning thee; directions that she should not be injured. 
 
It is ordinarily unwise to decide a case on the testimony of one party, especially one that is interested and likely to be strongly biassed in his own favor.

entries.title: II Samuel 14:9
segments: Iniquity be on me; the blame, if there was any, of his deciding that her son should not be slain.

entries.title: II Samuel 14:12
segments: Speak one word; having got David to decide that her son, who she said had killed his brother, should not be hurt, she wished now to make the application to Ablalom, sho had killed Amnon.

entries.title: II Samuel 14:13
segments:
Such a thing; more literally, a thing like this; that is, like what my family proposed to do in the case of my son. 
 
  Against the people of God; implying that David was injuring them by keeping Absalom in banishment, and having decided that her son should be spared, was faulty in not sparing his own son, and bringing him back from banishment. 
 
After persons are committed on the wrong side, those who are interested will endeavor to take advantage of that commitment to lead them still further into error and transgression.

entries.title: II Samuel 14:14
segments:
Yet doth he devise means; as God devises means to save men, and is ready to be reconciled to them, her implication was that David should be reconciled to Absalom. 
 
Those who so sympathize with murderers as to try to screen them from the punishment which God has directed, often refer to his mercy as a reason why his directions should not be followed; as if his justice were at war with his mercy, or as if they were more merciful than God.

entries.title: II Samuel 14:15
segments: The people have made me afraid; as she stated,

and she insinuated that there would be greater reason to fear the people, if Absalom should not be brought back, as they greatly desired it. 
 
  I will now speak unto the king; state a case as if it were her own, and then apply it to Absalom.

entries.title: II Samuel 14:17
segments: As an angel of God; wise and discerning.

entries.title: II Samuel 14:20
segments: To fetch about this form of speech; or, to change the face of this matter; that is, to give a new turn to the matter of Absalom's banishment.

entries.title: II Samuel 14:21
segments:
I have done this thing; he had decided, in the supposed case, that the woman's son should not be hurt, and was ready to make the desired application to Absalom. 
 
When rulers, through fear or favor, natural affection, or improper sympathy, fail to punish murderers, or pardon and receive them into favor, they take a course which tends to increase crime, and to bring upon themselves and others great distresses.

entries.title: II Samuel 14:22
segments: Grace; favor.

entries.title: II Samuel 14:25
segments: Men are prone to regard and be greatly influenced by mere external accomplishments, while the most beautiful form and graceful exterior may cover a polluted and murderous heart.

entries.title: II Samuel 14:26
segments: After the king's weight; some have thought this to be much less than the common shekel.

entries.title: II Samuel 14:30
segments: Connivance at crime, or an utterly inadequate punishment, tends to increase haughtiness, pride, and self-will in criminals, and to lead them on from one crime to another till they perish.

entries.title: II Samuel 14:33
segments: Parents who only kiss their children when they should punish them, have reason to fear that God, in righteous judgment, will suffer their children by their wickedness to become instruments of punishing their parents.
